name: ICL7660 Charge Pump Inverter
summary: Turns +5 V into -5 V with two capacitors and no inductor. The cheapest way to get a negative rail for an op-amp on a single-supply board.
notes: Two 10 uF capacitors and nothing else: one across CAP+ and CAP-, one from VOUT to ground. No inductor, no layout drama.
Output current is only about 20 mA, and the output sags as you draw it because the pump has real output impedance. It is for biasing op-amps and comparators, not for powering anything.

Default oscillator runs around 10 kHz, which lands squarely in the audio band. On the ICL7660S you can tie BOOST (pin 1) to V+ to push it to about 35 kHz. On any version you can hang a capacitor on OSC to move it deliberately.
LV (pin 6) should be grounded below 3.5 V supply and left open above it. Getting this backwards is the usual reason a 7660 works at 5 V and not at 3 V, or latches up at 9 V.
It can also double a voltage instead of inverting it, by rearranging the capacitors. The datasheet has the connection; it is not the default.
Absolute maximum is 10.5 V on the original ICL7660. The ICL7660S and ICL7660A take up to 12 V. The LM2662 delivers more current but only takes 5.5 V, so check the exact part before applying 12 V.

pins.name: NC
pins.note: Not connected on the ICL7660 and ICL7660A. Pin 1 is BOOST only on the ICL7660S, where tying it to V+ raises the oscillator to about 35 kHz, out of the audio band.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.note: Roughly minus the supply, minus the droop under load. 10 uF to ground here.

pins.name: LV
pins.note: Ground it below 3.5 V supply, leave open above. The wrong choice is why it works at one rail and not another.

pins.name: OSC
pins.note: A capacitor here slows the pump; an external clock overrides it.

pins.name: V+
pins.note: 10.5 V absolute maximum on the original part.

circuit.title: Negative supply

parts.why: The charge pump capacitor. This is the one that actually moves the charge across.
Reservoir on the output. Without it the negative rail is a sawtooth, not a supply.
LV bypasses the internal regulator below 3.5 V. Above 3.5 V it must be left open or the part can latch up.

circuit.note: Output impedance is around 55 ohms, so the negative rail sags under load: at 20 mA you lose more than a volt. It is a bias supply for op-amps and LCD contrast, not a power rail.
